attempts.sql: SELECT 'auto_ontology/server/' || regexp_extract(file_id, '^auto_ontology/server/([^/]+)/', 1) AS folder_path, SUM(line_count) AS total_lines FROM auto_ontology_code.code.files WHERE file_id LIKE 'auto_ontology/server/%' AND file_id LIKE '%.py' AND regexp_extract(file_id, '^auto_ontology/server/([^/]+)/', 1) <> '' GROUP BY regexp_extract(file_id, '^auto_ontology/server/([^/]+)/', 1) HAVING SUM(line_count) > 1000 ORDER BY total_lines DESC

Count every .py file anywhere inside the subfolder, including its test files and __init__.py; files directly in auto_ontology/server/ itself belong to no subfolder. Return the subfolder's repository-relative path (e.g. auto_ontology/server/chat) and its total line count.

Return exactly the requested output columns, using each requested name as the column alias, in the requested order. Return complete repository-relative file paths and complete symbol IDs exactly as stored. explanation: This sums Python line counts for all .py files under each immediate subfolder of auto_ontology/server/, including tests and __init__.py files. Files placed directly in auto_ontology/server/ are excluded because they do not belong to an immediate subfolder. The results show only subfolders whose total exceeds 1,000 lines, ordered by total lines descending.
sql: SELECT 'auto_ontology/server/' || regexp_extract(file_id, '^auto_ontology/server/([^/]+)/', 1) AS folder_path, SUM(line_count) AS total_lines FROM auto_ontology_code.code.files WHERE file_id LIKE 'auto_ontology/server/%' AND file_id LIKE '%.py' AND regexp_extract(file_id, '^auto_ontology/server/([^/]+)/', 1) <> '' GROUP BY regexp_extract(file_id, '^auto_ontology/server/([^/]+)/', 1) HAVING SUM(line_count) > 1000 ORDER BY total_lines DESC
